classes.note: Limited vote: 4 seats in each of the 47 mainland provinces (voters mark up to 3), 3 in Gran Canaria, Mallorca, and Tenerife (up to 2), 2 in Ceuta and Melilla, and 1 in each smaller island district, 208 in all; counted as 59 constituencies, with Ibiza and Formentera one district. Ley Orgánica 2/2026 (in force 2026-07-03) makes Formentera its own district, so 60 from the next general election. Senators designated by the regional parliaments are the class senado_autonomico.

classes.name: Investidura del Presidente del Gobierno
classes.disposition_reason: The Congreso invests the Prime Minister by a vote of its members (Constitution art. 99); regional presidents and mayors are chosen the same way by their chambers and councils (LOREG art. 196). These are parliamentary votes, not elections.

classes.name: Primarias de partidos
classes.disposition_reason: Parties run their own primaries under their statutes; the state neither administers nor publishes them.

classes.name: Elecciones sindicales y a cámaras agrarias
classes.name_en: Works council and agricultural chamber elections
classes.disposition_reason: Workplace representation (Estatuto de los Trabajadores) and agricultural chamber votes are professional and workplace ballots, not public elections.

classes.name: Elecciones a Cortes de la Segunda República
classes.note: Constituent Cortes 1931 and Cortes 1933 and 1936, elected by provincial and city constituencies with a majoritarian list vote and a second round where no list reached the threshold. The Congreso's historical deputies archive covers 1810-1977.

classes.name: Elecciones a Cortes, 1810-1923
classes.name_en: Cortes elections, 1810-1923 (Cádiz, Isabelline, Sexenio, and Restoration)
classes.note: From the Cortes of Cádiz to the 1923 election before Primo de Rivera's coup, mostly single-member districts with census or manhood suffrage (universal male from 1890). The Congreso's historical deputies archive lists members; vote counts sit in the Diario de Sesiones' actas.

classes.name: Procuradores en Cortes por el tercio familiar
classes.name_en: Family-representation members of the Francoist Cortes
classes.note: Two per province, elected by heads of family and married women in 1967 and 1971 under the Ley Orgánica del Estado (1967).

classes.name: Referéndums de 1947 y 1966
classes.name_en: Francoist referendums (1947 Succession Law, 1966 Organic Law of the State)
classes.note: Held under the Ley de Referéndum Nacional of 1945; results by province appear in the BOE proclamations.

classes.name: Elecciones a los parlamentos autonómicos
classes.note: Counted per constituency. Each statute of autonomy and regional electoral law sets the system: closed lists with D'Hondt and a 3-5% threshold, by province in most communities, by island in Canarias (plus a regional list since 2019) and Illes Balears, and one district in the single-province communities. The 13 communities that first voted on 8 May 1983 hold their elections on the fourth Sunday of May with the municipal elections unless their president dissolves early (LOREG art. 42.3); Andalucía, Cataluña, Galicia, and País Vasco keep their own calendars. Navarra's Parlamento Foral was first elected on 3 April 1979.

classes.note: Statutes of autonomy approved by referendum under art. 151 (Basque Country and Cataluña 1979, Galicia 1980, Andalucía 1981) and their reforms under art. 152.2 (Cataluña 2006, Andalucía 2007), plus Andalucía's autonomy-initiative referendum of 28 February 1980. classes.name: Elección de Diputados Provinciales
classes.name_en: Provincial councils (diputaciones), seat allocation by judicial district
classes.note: 38 common-regime provincial councils (25 to 51 members by population, art. 204): the provincial electoral board apportions seats to each judicial district, then to parties by D'Hondt on their municipal votes there, and the parties' councillors elect the deputies. None in the single-province communities or Navarra; the Basque provinces have juntas generales and the islands cabildos and consells. The ministry's type 10 files give the votes and seats by judicial district.

classes.name: Elecciones a los Consells Insulars
classes.note: Mallorca, Menorca, and Eivissa elect their consells directly since 2007, with the Balearic Parliament, closed lists by island (Ley 8/2007, then Ley 7/2009); Formentera's consell is also its municipal council and is elected under the LOREG's municipal rules. From 1979 to 2003 the consells were formed from each island's members of the Balearic Parliament.

classes.name: Elecciones municipales
classes.note: Counted per municipality with results in the ministry's files (05 and 11): closed lists with D'Hondt and 5% above 250 residents, open lists with a limited vote (5 seats, 4 marks) for 101-250, and 3 councillors for 100 or fewer since 2011. Mayors are then chosen by the council (art. 196). Ceuta and Melilla are their own class from 1995.

classes.name: Alcaldes de concejo abierto
classes.name_en: Directly elected mayors of open-council municipalities
classes.locator: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1985-11672 (art. 179.2: "En estos municipios los electores eligen directamente al Alcalde por sistema mayoritario")
classes.note: Municipalities governed by open council (LBRL art. 29: until 2011 every municipality under 100 residents, since Ley Orgánica 2/2011 only those that keep it by tradition or choice) elect only a mayor, by plurality, with the municipal elections. The open council of all residents then governs.

cadence.locator: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1985-11672 (art. 42.3: "Las elecciones se realizan el cuarto domingo de mayo del año que corresponda y los mandatos, de cuatro años, terminan en todo caso el día anterior al de la celebración de las siguientes elecciones")

classes.name: Consultas populares municipales
classes.locator: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1985-5392 (art. 71: the mayor may call a popular consultation with the council's absolute majority and the national Government's authorization)
classes.note: Rare and ad hoc; the Government authorizes each one. Catalan municipal consultations under the Generalitat's own laws and the 2014 and 2017 Catalan votes are not referendums under art. 71 (the 2014 and 2017 ones were suspended and annulled by the Constitutional Court).

classes.name: Elecciones a alcaldes pedáneos y juntas vecinales (entidades locales menores)
classes.name_en: Sub-municipal entities: pedáneo mayors, neighborhood boards, and Navarre concejos
classes.locator: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1985-11672 (art. 199.2: "Los Alcaldes Pedáneos son elegidos directamente por los vecinos de la correspondiente entidad local por sistema mayoritario")
classes.note: The pedáneo mayor of each entidad local menor is elected by plurality with the municipal elections; the board's members are apportioned from the municipal votes in the entity's sections (art. 199), unless the community's own law says otherwise (Navarra's concejos, Asturias's parroquias rurales). Most are in Castilla y León (León, Burgos, Palencia), Navarra, Cantabria, Galicia, and Extremadura.

classes.name: Elecciones municipales, 1835-1973
classes.name_en: Municipal elections before 1979 (liberal, Restoration, Republic, and Francoist family-third councillors)
classes.note: Liberal and Restoration councils from the 1835 and 1877 municipal laws; the 12 April 1931 elections that brought the Second Republic, with partial ones in 1931 and 1933; and the councillors elected by heads of family under Franco (1948-1973). No national file; the 1931 results sit in provincial gazettes and the Anuario Estadístico.
